title: Eleven Days Over the Open Ocean: The Journey a Bird Cannot Skip
title_zh: 飞越开阔洋面的十一天：鸟儿无法跳过的旅程
intro_zh: 本文约 535 词，围绕“候鸟为什么要长途迁徙”展开，从食物与日照变化、遗传本能、能量储备、导航方式、追踪手段与栖息地流失六个角度说明这场旅程的代价与逻辑，含 6 个 CET-4 核心词，句子难度中等，理解目标约 85%-90%。

paragraphs.en: Each September, a small brown shorebird called the bar-tailed godwit leaves Alaska and flies south over open ocean. It does not stop for food or rest. About eleven days and 11,000 kilometers later, it lands in New Zealand, thinner but alive. No aircraft could make that trip without refueling. The bird does it on a body that weighs less than a bag of sugar. Why would any animal spend so much energy on a journey?
paragraphs.zh: 每年九月，一种名叫斑尾塍鹬的棕色小型涉禽离开阿拉斯加，向南飞越开阔的洋面。它中途不停下来觅食，也不休息。大约十一天、11000 公里之后，它降落在新西兰，瘦了些，但还活着。没有哪架飞机会在不加油的情况下完成这趟航程。而这只鸟靠的是一个比一袋糖还轻的身体。为什么会有动物把这么多能量花在一段旅程上呢？

paragraphs.en: Staying would be worse. In winter the insects and worms that feed most birds disappear under snow or frozen ground, and daylight falls to a few hours — too little time to find a meal. Flying to a warmer place is not an adventure; it is the cheaper choice. The signal is often simple: shorter days change hormone levels, and the bird grows restless and begins to migrate.
paragraphs.zh: 留下来反而更糟。冬天，多数鸟类赖以为生的昆虫和蠕虫消失在积雪或冻土之下，白昼缩短到只有几个小时——根本不够找一顿吃的。飞往更温暖的地方不是一场冒险，而是一个更划算的选择。触发信号往往很简单：变短的白昼改变了激素水平，鸟变得躁动不安，于是开始迁徙。

paragraphs.en: Nobody teaches them the route. Young cuckoos hatch in summer and fly south weeks after their parents have already gone; they have never seen the way. This is instinct — a program written into their genes by thousands of generations of birds that made the trip and survived. Birds raised alone in cages, with no adult to copy, still turn their bodies south when autumn comes.
paragraphs.zh: 没有人教它们路线。幼杜鹃在夏天孵出，在父母早已南去数周之后才独自南飞；它们从未见过那条路。这就是本能——是成千上万代完成过旅程并活下来的鸟写进基因里的一套程序。独自养在笼中、没有成鸟可模仿的鸟，到了秋天依然会把身体转向南方。

paragraphs.en: Long flights need fuel. Before departure many birds eat almost without stopping and can nearly double their weight in fat. Their hearts and flight muscles grow larger at the same time, while some even shrink their digestive organs to save energy and rebuild them after landing. Some arrive having burned nearly half their starting weight. Fat is the tank; a smaller gut is the luggage left behind.
paragraphs.zh: 长途飞行需要燃料。出发前，许多鸟几乎不停地进食，体重可以因脂肪而接近翻倍。与此同时它们的心脏和飞行肌肉会变大，有些鸟甚至会缩小消化器官以节省能量，落地后再重新长回来。有的鸟抵达时几乎烧掉了出发时一半的体重。脂肪是油箱，缩小的肠道是被留在家的行李。

paragraphs.en: Finding the way is a second problem. Birds navigate by reading the sun by day and the stars by night, and they can correct for the sun's slow movement across the sky. They also sense the Earth's magnetic field, follow coastlines and rivers, and some may even use smell. In one classic experiment, birds kept from seeing the stars on clear nights grew confused once the sky turned cloudy.
paragraphs.zh: 找到方向是第二个难题。鸟类靠白天读太阳、夜晚读星辰来导航，并且能够校正太阳在天空中缓慢移动带来的误差。它们还能感知地球磁场，沿着海岸线和河流飞行，有些甚至可能借助气味。在一项经典实验中，被阻止在晴夜看星星的鸟，一旦天空转阴便迷了路。

paragraphs.en: Scientists learned much of this by tagging. A tiny ring on the leg, or a satellite tag lighter than a coin, sends back the bird's position. One bar-tailed godwit was tracked for eleven years, flying the same route again and again, always arriving within a few days of the same date. Some birds are now followed hour by hour, which has turned migration from a mystery into a map.
paragraphs.zh: 科学家很大程度上是通过给鸟做标记了解到这些的。腿上一枚小小的环，或者一枚比硬币还轻的卫星标签，就能发回鸟的位置。有一只斑尾塍鹬被追踪了十一年，一次次飞同一条路线，每次抵达的日期相差不过几天。如今有些鸟能被逐小时跟踪，迁徙由谜团变成了一张地图。

paragraphs.en: The journey is hard to endure. Storms blow birds far off course; hawks wait at resting places; a single lost wetland can mean a failed flight. The mudflats of the Yellow Sea, where millions of birds refuel each spring, have declined by about a third in thirty years. Each stopping place is a link in a chain, and one broken link matters.
paragraphs.zh: 这段旅程很难忍受。风暴把鸟吹离航线，鹰隼在休息地守候，失去一片湿地就可能意味着一趟失败的飞行。黄海的泥滩是数百万只鸟每年春天补充能量的地方，三十年间已减少约三分之一。每一个停歇地都是链条上的一环，而断掉一环就意味着问题。

paragraphs.en: So migration is not a holiday in the sun. It is a calculated risk: the bird trades danger and enormous energy for the chance to eat all winter and return home to breed. When a V of geese crosses a grey October sky, you are watching an animal answer an old question — leave, or starve — with the same answer its ancestors gave.
paragraphs.zh: 所以迁徙并不是去阳光下度假。它是一场精打细算的冒险：鸟用自己的危险和巨大能量，换取整个冬天有饭吃、并能回家繁殖的机会。当一队排成人字形的大雁掠过十月灰蒙蒙的天空时，你看到的是一只动物在回答一个古老的问题——走，还是饿死——而它给出的答案与祖辈一模一样。

questions.q: According to the passage, why do most birds leave their summer homes?
options: To escape from hunters and predators
To follow their parents to a fixed place
Because food grows scarce and daylight is too short
To collect new materials for their nests
questions.explain: 细节题。第二段明确指出：冬天昆虫和蠕虫消失，白昼缩短到只有几个小时，找不到食物，因此飞往温暖处是更划算的选择，故选第三项。第一项、第四项文中未提，第二项与第三段幼杜鹃独自南飞相矛盾。

questions.q: The word "instinct" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to
options: a skill learned by watching adults
a natural ability present from birth
a habit formed through daily practice
a memory passed on by a single parent
questions.explain: 词义题。第三段说没人教它们路线，幼鸟从未见过那条路，笼中单独长大的鸟仍会南飞，可见 instinct 指与生俱来的天生能力，故选第二项；第一、三项强调后天学习与练习，与原文相反。

questions.q: What can be inferred about stopover sites such as the Yellow Sea mudflats?
options: Their loss can threaten the whole migration route
They are the birds' final destination each year
Birds stay there for only a few hours
They are now protected by international law
questions.explain: 推断题。第七段说每个停歇地都是链条上的一环，断掉一环就意味着问题，而黄海泥滩三十年间减少约三分之一，可推出停歇地消失会威胁整条迁徙路线，故选第一项。第二项错误，终点是新西兰等地；第三、四项文中没有依据。

questions.q: What does the author mean by calling migration "a calculated risk"?
options: Birds learn their routes by trial and error
Birds accept danger and high energy costs in exchange for food and breeding
Migration is a kind of game played by young birds
Birds migrate only when the weather is fine
questions.explain: 句意/主旨题。末段解释：鸟用危险和巨大能量换取整个冬天有食物、并能回家繁殖的机会，这正是权衡得失后的冒险，故选第二项。第一、四项与文中本能、导航等内容不符；第三项曲解了 calculated risk 的意思。
